question: A 64-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of intractable hiccups and shortness of breath on exertion. He also has a 1-month history of left shoulder pain. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Physical examination shows decreased breath sounds at the left lung base. An x-ray of the chest shows a 3-cm perihilar mass and elevation of the left hemidiaphragm. This patient's symptoms are most likely caused by injury to a nerve that also innervates which of the following structures?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Phrenic nerve injury -> decreased diaphragmatic movement -> elevation of left hemidiaphragm -> 80% CHAIN: Phrenic nerve innervates diaphragm and pericardium -> injury can affect fibrous pericardium -> 70% CHAIN: Phrenic nerve innervates diaphragm and mediastinal pleura -> injury can affect visceral pleura -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of intractable hiccups, shortness of breath, left shoulder pain, and physical exam findings of decreased breath sounds and chest x-ray findings of a perihilar mass and elevated left hemidiaphragm are suggestive of a Pancoast tumor, which is a type of lung cancer that involves the apex of the lung. The symptoms are likely caused by injury to the phrenic nerve, which innervates the diaphragm. The phrenic nerve also innervates the pericardium, so the symptoms are most likely caused by injury to a nerve that also innervates the fibrous pericardium.
